title: Neo: Towards Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption Acceleration using Tensor Core
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) imposes massive computational overhead—orders of magnitude over plaintext computation—that prevents practical deployment, while existing ASIC accelerators lack generality as FHE algorithms rapidly evolve. GPU-based solutions exist but fail to exploit tensor core (TCU) hardware for the dominant FHE primitives.
motivation: FHE enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data, but its performance gap vs. plaintext is too large for real-world use; exploiting the high throughput of Tensor Cores on modern GPUs is a promising path to close this gap without sacrificing generality.
method: Neo takes the CKKS encryption scheme (a way to compute on encrypted data without decrypting it) and reformulates its two main computational bottlenecks—the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT, a fast algorithm for multiplying encrypted polynomials) and polynomial multiplication—as matrix operations. GPU Tensor Cores (specialized hardware within GPUs) can then accelerate these operations using 8-bit integer or 16-bit floating-point math. To fit onto Tensor Cores, the design breaks the NTT into smaller stages (butterfly stages) matching the Tensor Core's matrix dimensions and uses residue number system arithmetic (an encoding that prevents overflow in low-precision math). Custom code handles data arrangement, twiddle factor injection (rotation constants used in NTT), and modular reduction to keep everything within precision limits.
key_novelty: The core idea is reformulating encrypted polynomial arithmetic (NTT and residue number system multiplication in CKKS) as matrix multiplication, so GPUs' specialized Tensor Core hardware can accelerate cryptographic calculations instead of using general-purpose GPU cores.
contributions: TCU-based acceleration of NTT and polynomial multiplication for the CKKS FHE scheme
Custom kernel design mapping FHE polynomial arithmetic to INT8/FP16 matrix operations within GPU tensor cores
Analysis of precision requirements and modular arithmetic constraints to preserve correctness under low-precision TCU computation
Performance evaluation demonstrating GPGPU FHE acceleration with Tensor Core utilization

limitations: Not discussed; generality to other FHE schemes (BGV, BFV) beyond CKKS is not established from the abstract.
